prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, and the first experimental demonstration of the quantum spin Hall state

statement.case_for: Topological insulators are a new class of quantum matter whose existence follows from band structure plus spin-orbit coupling. Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall prediction. Molenkamp's group then measured quantized edge conductance in HgTe wells, so the chain from prediction to verified measurement is complete. The result has been confirmed independently for more than fifteen years, in HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi-based compounds and three-dimensional materials, by transport and by ARPES. First-principles electronic-structure theory now predicts candidate topological materials routinely, so the idea has changed how we compute and search for materials, and I can speak to that from my own field. It is a clear, verified physical discovery, it supports the broader message that quantum mechanics keeps producing surprises, and the recognition is timely.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang was what made the experiment possible, and Zhang is now deceased. The three-dimensional topological insulator work of Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents and Hasan sits partly outside the credited names. A three-person cap leaves a visible gap on the theory side. There is also an argument that the 2016 prize for topological phases already recognised the field, and that practical applications of quantum spin Hall edge channels remain modest.

responses.point: Goran Johansson ranked B038 only eighth, deferring to condensed-matter colleagues. He noted that the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a concern and that the 2016 prize on topological phases makes the novelty of this discovery a judgment call.
responses.response: I take the attribution point seriously and have no neat answer to it. I still think the three names are the most defensible allocation. Kane and Mele made the symmetry-based prediction, and Molenkamp made the first measurement that confirmed it. The BHZ proposal sharpened the choice of material, but the concept and the first experimental proof are what the citation should centre on, and Zhang's death removes one of the hardest conflicts. On 2016, I disagree that it covers this work. The Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz prize honoured topological invariants in quantum Hall states and in phase transitions, which broke time-reversal symmetry or concerned defects. Time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators are a distinct discovery with their own materials-science consequences. I would still welcome the chair's guidance on how wide the citation should be.

responses.point: Stefan Kroll ranked optical lattice clocks first. He cites accuracy near 1e-18, a new measurement capability (geodesy, dark-matter searches, a redefinition of the second) and independent confirmation by many laboratories, with Katori and Ye as a clean two-person credit.
responses.response: I agree that B046 is a strong candidate. The confirmation is independent, the credit is clean, and the performance is measured rather than argued. It is my second alternative. My difference with Stefan is about the type of discovery. The clock is a spectacular instrument advance, but I rank a prediction that was then verified as a new state of matter slightly higher, because it changes what we understand about materials. The overlap Stefan raises with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is also real, since Ye already shares the 2005 prize for the frequency comb. I would not put B046 behind B038 for lack of merit. I place it there because B038 has the cleaner conceptual novelty.

responses.point: Bernhard Mehlig ranked twisted bilayer graphene third and flagged that the credit is a clean theory-plus-experiment pair but that priority for the flat-band idea is shared with earlier theorists and the superconducting pairing mechanism is unresolved. He ranked defect-mediated 2D melting first.
responses.response: I share his doubt about B042 and ranked it second for that reason. The phenomena are reproduced in many laboratories, but without a settled mechanism a citation would have to be carefully limited to the prediction of flat bands and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity. That is possible, though I suspect a few more years would make the interpretation and the credit cleaner. On B036, I find the physics elegant and the confirmation by colloids and films credible. My difficulty is that the KTHNY scenario is not universally confirmed (first-order melting appears in several systems), and it sits right next to the 2016 prize through Kosterlitz and Thouless. On the 2016 point I am therefore harder on B036 than on B038, because the topological-defect concepts were exactly what that prize honoured.

responses.point: Ulf Danielsson supports B038 as a coherent theory-plus-experiment trio confirmed by many groups, and ranked it third. He notes that Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D contributors are legitimate competing claimants and that the 2016 prize may be cited as overlap.
responses.response: I agree with Ulf's reading and thank him for naming the 3D contributors, since the three-person structure of the prize cannot represent them. My view is that the 2D quantum spin Hall effect is the cleaner core. The 3D topological insulator claim involves more contributors and could be handled by a citation that does not claim to cover everything. Where I differ slightly is on B051: WMAP is certainly mature, but the 2006 and 2019 prizes recognised closely related cosmology, and I defer to him on the physics. I would be glad if he would say whether he considers the allocation within WMAP more or less contested than Kane-Mele-Molenkamp.

uncertainties: Whether a citation limited to the quantum spin Hall effect in two dimensions can be defended without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, or whether the committee should word it more broadly.
Whether the committee will see B038 as already covered by the 2016 topological-phases prize, a point that colleagues have raised and that I answered only on conceptual grounds.
Whether B042 gains enough clarity about the superconducting mechanism to displace B038 in the final ranking; I recall details of the credit history from memory and have not verified them.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I work in theoretical condensed matter and electronic-structure theory, and I have no known collaboration or institutional link to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Katori or Ye. My long-standing interest in topological-materials prediction by DFT is a scientific bias that I declare, not a recusal ground.
